title: Week 4: Cut the cord
summary: The last step: an Anker 20,000 mAh battery powers the Pi and the servos, so your robot runs with no cables at all. Then take it for a walk and show it off.
detail: Mount the battery pack in the base, move the Pi and servo power onto it, and check it all still runs. Then the robot is fully wireless: pick it up, carry it across the room and keep talking. We finish with a show-and-tell and a group video.
outcome: A finished cardboard robot that runs anywhere on its own battery, listening, talking, moving its mouth and turning its head.
artifact: A fully wireless talking cardboard robot, and a clip of it out in the world.
prereqs: Your robot from Week 3, with its Raspberry Pi.
On your table: an Anker 20,000 mAh power bank and its cables.

slides.title: Week 4: Cut the cord
bullets: Then pick it up and walk around with it.

slides.title: What each robot needs this week
bullets: ☐ Your robot from Week 3, with its Pi, speakerphone and Pico
☐ The Anker 20,000 mAh power bank from Week 2, fully charged
☐ 1 × short USB-C to USB-C cable, battery to Pi
☐ The servo power lead from Week 2
☐ Velcro strips or tape, to hold the battery in the base
Bring: your laptop and your Deepgram key
slides.note: The Pi 4 wants a steady 3 A. If a Pi shows a lightning bolt or restarts on battery, swap to a port marked for higher power or a thicker cable. Helper table: spare charged power banks, spare short USB-C cables, a phone tripod for the show-and-tell video.

slides.title: Mount the battery
bullets: Charge check: press the button on the power bank, all lights should show.
Slide the battery into the base box, behind the neck servo.
Tape it down so it can't slide when the head turns.
slides.note: The battery is the heaviest part, so low in the base keeps the robot from tipping.

slides.title: Move the power over
bullets: Pi power cable from the battery's USB-C port.
Servo power lead from the battery's other port.
Unplug the wall supply. Everything should keep running.
slides.note: Done when: the wall plug is out and the robot still answers.

slides.title: Take it for a walk
bullets: Carry it to another table and have a conversation.
Film a clip and share it with #RobotLunchLab.
Vote for best personality, best voice and best build.
slides.note: Wrap up: thank everyone for four weeks. Robots go home with their builders.

flow.title: Final test, unplugged
flow.note: Open this page on the robot's Pi. Unplug every cable, then start talking.

troubleshooting: The Pi restarts when the head moves: the Pi and servos are pulling too much from one port. Use separate ports on the battery.
The Pi shows a lightning bolt: the battery is low or the cable is thin. Charge the battery or swap the cable.
The battery switches itself off: some power banks sleep on low current. Press its button to wake it.
